SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #8
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SOCIAL STUDIES
TIME ALLOWED: 90 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 80
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. What does the letter E stand for on a compass rose? (1 mark)
   A. Earth
   B. Equator
   C. Edge
   D. East

2. Where does the sun set? (1 mark)
   A. In the east
   B. In the north
   C. In the south
   D. In the west

3. Which direction is Mombasa from Nairobi on a map of Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. West
   B. North
   C. South-east
   D. North-west

4. Which is the highest mountain in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Aberdare Range
   B. Ngong Hills
   C. Mount Kenya
   D. Mount Elgon

5. Which lake is the largest lake in Africa and is shared by Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania? (1 mark)
   A. Lake Victoria
   B. Lake Baringo
   C. Lake Nakuru
   D. Lake Naivasha

6. Which clothing helps drivers to see you on a rainy day? (1 mark)
   A. Bright or reflective clothes
   B. Dark grey clothes
   C. Black clothes
   D. Brown clothes

7. Which clothing is most suitable in the cold season? (1 mark)
   A. Light shorts only
   B. Swimming costumes
   C. Sandals only
   D. Sweaters and jackets

8. What is weather? (1 mark)
   A. The number of months in a year
   B. How the air is on a particular day
   C. The height of a mountain
   D. The size of a county

9. Which disease can spread more easily in wet weather because mosquitoes breed in puddles? (1 mark)
   A. Broken leg
   B. Malaria
   C. Toothache
   D. Sunburn

10. What is the name of the organisation that looks after most museums in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Kenya Airways
   B. Kenya Ports
   C. National Museums of Kenya
   D. Kenya Power

11. Which pattern describes each family living far from the next on its own land? (1 mark)
   A. Crowded
   B. Scattered
   C. Clustered
   D. Linear

12. Which of these counties has a very dense city population? (1 mark)
   A. Nairobi
   B. Turkana
   C. Marsabit
   D. Wajir

13. Which is a reason why many people live in towns? (1 mark)
   A. No roads
   B. No water
   C. Jobs, shops and services
   D. No schools

14. Which houses in Lamu were built with coral stone? (1 mark)
   A. Old town houses
   B. Boats
   C. Tents
   D. Round grass houses

15. Which is a good manner when interviewing an elder about culture? (1 mark)
   A. Greeting politely and asking permission to record
   B. Interrupting
   C. Laughing
   D. Refusing to listen

16. Why do schools have rules? (1 mark)
   A. To stop friendship
   B. To stop lessons
   C. To keep everyone safe and help learning
   D. To make pupils sad

17. Why is it important to check facts before telling your school's history? (1 mark)
   A. So that it is funny
   B. So that what you tell is true
   C. So that nobody listens
   D. So that the story is longer

18. Which item of clothing protects a worker's head in a factory? (1 mark)
   A. Scarf
   B. Sandals
   C. Helmet
   D. Skirt

19. Which of these is a right of a school citizen? (1 mark)
   A. To steal
   B. To bully others
   C. To break rules
   D. To learn in a safe place

20. In an essay on good citizenship, what should the beginning say? (1 mark)
   A. A recipe
   B. What a good citizen is
   C. A list of foods
   D. The weather report

21. What is a peace garden? (1 mark)
   A. A place for fighting
   B. A market
   C. A car park
   D. A garden where pupils can sit and be calm

22. Which is a peace message? (1 mark)
   A. Shout louder
   B. Get back at them
   C. Fight for it
   D. Talk, do not fight

23. How often are general elections held in Kenya? (1 mark)
   A. Every month
   B. Every ten years
   C. Every five years
   D. Every year

24. Which shows respect for the minority? (1 mark)
   A. Laughing at them
   B. Ignoring them
   C. Listening to those who did not win
   D. Sending them away

25. What should a Children's Government NOT do? (1 mark)
   A. Organise clean-up days
   B. Represent pupils
   C. Punish other pupils by itself
   D. Welcome visitors

26. What does a class representative do? (1 mark)
   A. Brings the ideas and complaints of classmates to the meeting
   B. Cooks food
   C. Punishes pupils
   D. Teaches lessons

27. Which of these is a way of participating in the Children's Government? (1 mark)
   A. Voting for leaders
   B. Breaking rules
   C. Ignoring elections
   D. Laughing at leaders

28. What is the meaning of composition of a group? (1 mark)
   A. The colour of the group
   B. The size of the room
   C. The song of the group
   D. The people or parts that make up the group

29. What happens when leaders are dishonest? (1 mark)
   A. Trust is lost and resources are wasted
   B. People are happier
   C. The community grows faster
   D. Nothing changes

30. Which of these leads prayers in a mosque? (1 mark)
   A. A cook
   B. An imam
   C. A tailor
   D. A nurse

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
31. List the steps for solving a conflict peacefully. (4 marks)

32. Give two traditional foods and say where each is popular. (4 marks)

33. Name two water features found in Kenya. (2 marks)

34. Give three things that should be on a sketch map of your county. (3 marks)

35. Explain what neighbouring counties are. (2 marks)

36. Explain the meaning of profit and show how to find it. (3 marks)

37. Describe how an ordinary pupil can support the Children's Government. (3 marks)

38. Explain why discipline is important in school. (3 marks)

39. What is meant by a densely populated area? (2 marks)

40. Describe how a losing candidate should behave and why. (3 marks)

41. Explain how the four seasons can influence what people do in your county. Give one example for each season. (5 marks)

42. What is the difference between a lake and a river? (2 marks)

43. Describe two peace-building activities that a school can carry out. (4 marks)

44. Name the two main parts of a county government and state what each does. (4 marks)

45. How do you calculate profit? (2 marks)

46. Describe the houses of two communities in Kenya. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
SOCIAL STUDIES — MOCK EXAM #8 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — East
   E is the short form of east.

2. D — In the west
   The sun sets in the west.

3. C — South-east
   Mombasa lies to the south-east of Nairobi.

4. C — Mount Kenya
   Mount Kenya is the highest mountain in Kenya.

5. A — Lake Victoria
   Lake Victoria is shared by three countries.

6. A — Bright or reflective clothes
   Bright and reflective clothes stand out.

7. D — Sweaters and jackets
   Warm clothing keeps us comfortable when it is cold.

8. B — How the air is on a particular day
   Weather describes sun, rain, wind and temperature at a given time.

9. B — Malaria
   Mosquitoes that spread malaria breed in standing water.

10. C — National Museums of Kenya
   The National Museums of Kenya manages many museums.

11. B — Scattered
   Scattered means spread widely apart.

12. A — Nairobi
   Nairobi has a large city population.

13. C — Jobs, shops and services
   Towns offer work and services.

14. A — Old town houses
   Old Lamu houses used coral stone.

15. A — Greeting politely and asking permission to record
   Politeness shows respect.

16. C — To keep everyone safe and help learning
   Rules protect people and help learning.

17. B — So that what you tell is true
   History must be accurate.

18. C — Helmet
   Helmets protect workers' heads.

19. D — To learn in a safe place
   Learning safely is a right.

20. B — What a good citizen is
   The introduction gives the main idea.

21. D — A garden where pupils can sit and be calm
   A peace garden is calm and beautiful.

22. D — Talk, do not fight
   Talking solves problems peacefully.

23. C — Every five years
   Kenya holds general elections every five years.

24. C — Listening to those who did not win
   Democracy includes everyone.

25. C — Punish other pupils by itself
   Only teachers decide on discipline.

26. A — Brings the ideas and complaints of classmates to the meeting
   Class representatives speak for their classmates.

27. A — Voting for leaders
   Voting is part of participating.

28. D — The people or parts that make up the group
   Composition means the members that make up a group.

29. A — Trust is lost and resources are wasted
   Dishonesty harms the community.

30. B — An imam
   An imam leads prayers.

SECTION B
----
31. (4 marks)
   Answer: Stop, calm down, talk and listen, find a solution together, and say sorry and forgive.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct step, up to 4.

32. (4 marks)
   Answer: For example: githeri in central Kenya and fish with ugali near Lake Victoria. Accept other correct examples.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each food and 1 mark for each correct place.

33. (2 marks)
   Answer: Lake Victoria and the Tana River. Accept Lake Turkana, Lake Naivasha or the Indian Ocean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct feature.

34. (3 marks)
   Answer: A title, a north arrow and a key. Accept sub-county names and boundaries.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct item.

35. (2 marks)
   Answer: Neighbouring counties are counties that share a boundary with your county.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for sharing a boundary, 1 mark for saying they are next to yours.

36. (3 marks)
   Answer: Profit is the money left after all costs are paid. Profit = income - costs.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for meaning, 1 mark for formula, 1 mark for correct example.

37. (3 marks)
   Answer: Vote for leaders, follow fair instructions, and give ideas through the class representative.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

38. (3 marks)
   Answer: It keeps the school orderly, it helps everyone learn, and it prepares us to be good citizens.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

39. (2 marks)
   Answer: An area where many people live close together.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for many people, 1 mark for close together.

40. (3 marks)
   Answer: Accept the result peacefully, congratulate the winner and offer to help. This keeps peace and shows respect for democracy.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

41. (5 marks)
   Answer: Rainy: farmers plant crops. Dry: farmers harvest and dry crops. Hot: people drink more water and wear light clothes. Cold: people wear warm clothes and drink hot tea. Award a fifth mark for a clear explanation of why seasons matter for farming.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each season example and 1 mark for the link to activities.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: A lake is a large area of water with land around it. A river is water flowing along a channel to a lake or ocean.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct description.

43. (4 marks)
   Answer: A peace garden where pupils can sit calmly and a peace poster competition to teach about peace. Explain how each helps.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each activity and 1 mark for each explanation.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: The county executive runs the county and carries out laws. The county assembly makes county laws and checks the executive.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each part and 1 mark for each job.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: Profit is found by subtracting the costs from the income.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for subtracting, 1 mark for costs from income.

46. (4 marks)
   Answer: The Maasai build low houses of wooden frames covered with mud and dung inside a fence called a manyatta. Old coastal houses in Lamu were built of coral stone with carved doors.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each community and 1 mark for each description.
